judged_text: The fallback branch of selectedCalendar in updateEvent is a dead lookup that can never match, and the same defect is duplicated in deleteEvent (lines 312-315). When externalCalendarId is null/empty (bookings whose BookingReference stored no externalCalendarId), the code executes event.destinationCalendar?.find((cal) => cal.externalId === externalCalendarId)?.externalId, where externalCalendarId is falsy so the find never matches and the expression is always undefined; calendarId becomes undefined and the Google events.update/events.delete call targets no calendar, so reschedules and cancellations of pre-existing bookings fail against Google's API and the remote event is left orphaned on the user's calendar — a regression from the old behavior which fell back to event.destinationCalendar?.externalId.

adjudication.rationale: In `packages/app-store/googlecalendar/lib/CalendarService.ts`, both `updateEvent` and `deleteEvent` changed the fallback calendar selection to `event.destinationCalendar?.find((cal) => cal.externalId === externalCalendarId)?.externalId` when `externalCalendarId` is falsy. Since that branch only runs when `externalCalendarId` is null/undefined/empty, the predicate compares `cal.externalId` to a falsy value and will almost always never match, yielding `undefined`. This is a verifiable logic defect introduced by the diff and is duplicated in `deleteEvent` (the `calendarId` assignment). The old behavior fell back to the destination calendar’s externalId; the new code does not.
